messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected for customer Equinox on Dedicated cluster equinox-prod-pool. 5xx rate = 12% over the last 5m. Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-5xx. Paging on-call now. Context: errors are primarily gateway 502/503 and some connection resets. (auto-detected at 09:14 UTC)

alex: on it. seen a couple of spikes in GPU mem pressure earlier. will grab ingress logs + pool metrics.

morgan: thx alex. I'm standing by for impact. cust-success-sam DMed customer that we're investigating.

alex: quick dump from router logs (filtered for equinox tenant, last 3m):
```
[09:12:30] proxy: upstream returned 503 code=EVICT_STREAM tenant=equinox trace=abc123
[09:13:01] proxy: connection reset by peer tenant=equinox backend=worker-12
[09:13:14] gateway: 502 gateway_error model=redwood-gpt-q4 seq_len=1024
```
Looks like backend worker-side failures, not just proxy.

jia: checking autoscaler & pool metrics now. cpu/gpu and queue depth.

jia: autoscaler didn't spin up beyond reserved capacity. pool config shows: min=6, max=8, burst_capacity disabled for equinox-prod-pool. scaling events: none in last 20m. GPU mem utilization on nodes: 98% on two hosts (worker-11, worker-12). KV cache evictions spiked.

pranay: noisy neighbor signs — single tenant task pattern continuous long prefix generation? any long-running calls?

alex: yes, I see repeated long generation jobs on tenant 'equinox-fn-internal' hitting seq_len ~ 4096 with large batch sizes. Those requests are holding KV cache and causing other requests to OOM/evict.

cust-success-sam: update from Equinox: they reported higher end-user errors on /api/rerank and /api/summary starting ~09:05 UTC. Business impact: degraded UX on key flows. They need ETA.

morgan: mitigation proposal 1) temporarily throttle max tokens for equinox-fn-internal 2) enable bursting (increase pool to +2 nodes) 3) reroute a subset to hosted fallback model. which is fastest to implement?

alex: fastest: per-tenant rate limit toggle + temporary routing to hosted fallback. I'll open an emergency routing change.

pranay: how about reducing batch size at the frontend for that tenant to avoid long tail memory usage? low friction too.

alex: doing three things in parallel:
- apply per-tenant rate limit for equinox-fn-internal to 60rps
- reduce default batch size for that tenant from 16 -> 4
- create a routing rule to divert 20% of traffic for /api/rerank -> hosted model redwood-llama-q4-1 (higher latency, lower error)

alex: applying rate limit now...
```bash
# api call to control plane (ACL)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/equinox/limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"max_rps":60,"scope":"equinox-fn-internal"}'
```

deploy-bot: config-change: tenant-rate-limit applied by alex (change-id: cfg-821).

alex: batch size change applied to routing layer (config push id: push-542).

deploy-bot: config-change: batch-size updated for equinox-fn-internal by alex (push-542).

alex: creating routing rule to send 20% of rerank traffic to hosted fallback.

deploy-bot: routing-change: rule eqx-fallback-20% applied (rb-77).

morgan: monitoring metrics. can you share short curl to verify fallback path?

alex: quick health check to exercise reroute:
```bash
curl -H "X-Tenant: equinox" -X POST https://api.redwood/proxy/rerank -d '{"items":[...]}'
# expect header X-Backend: hosted/redwood-llama-q4-1 when rerouted
```

alex: initial checks: overall 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 6% in 4m after rate limit + batch reduction + 20% reroute. success but still above baseline.

jia: autoscaler note: burst_capacity was disabled due to tenant quota. we can flip it but need approval from infra. flipping would allow pool to scale to 10 nodes.

pranay: manual scale +2 nodes if infra gives thumbs. that'll reduce pressure and restore KV cache hit rate.

morgan: I'm ok with manual scale. alex, can you request infra? I'll loop infra.

alex: pinging infra-team (cc @matt-infra).

alex: infra approved emergency manual scale +2 nodes, initiating.

deploy-bot: infra-action: manual-scale equinox-prod-pool +2 nodes initiated by alex (op-998).

jia: watching node provisioning. KV eviction rate trending down after scale kicks in. queue depth reduced.

cust-success-sam: passed ETA to customer: mitigation in progress, errors reduced but some endpoints still impacted. Keeping them updated every 15m.

morgan: can we confirm the root cause as: long-running large-prefix generations from equinox-fn-internal causing KV cache thrash -> GPU mem pressure -> worker OOMs -> 502/503 for other tenant requests?

alex: that's the working hypothesis supported by logs and metrics. notable evidence: high seq_len requests, large batch sizes, eviction spikes coincident with 5xx surges.

pranay: add a temporary quota on max sequence length for that tenant to stop the long tails. That should be quick and low friction.

alex: applied seq_len cap: 2048 for equinox-fn-internal (cfg-824).

deploy-bot: config-change: seq_len-cap applied (cfg-824).

jia: node join complete. pool size now +2. GPU mem per-host dropped to ~63%. KV eviction rate down 85% vs peak. 5xx now at 2.1% in last 2m.

cust-success-sam: passed update to Equinox: errors back to near baseline for most flows, still monitoring /api/rerank for tail. Customer appreciated the quick response.

morgan: great. start drafting incident timeline and impact. who wants handoff to next on-call?

alex: logging final actions and metrics here, handing off to morgan (oncall-next) for night watch and postmortem.

morgan: taking handoff. next steps for postmortem:
- correlate request traces for equinox-fn-internal to find why they started sending long seq_len
- recommend permanent limits or quotas and enable burst_capacity with quota safeguards
- evaluate autoscaler thresholds that prevented earlier scale-up
- customer follow-up note from cust-success-sam with root cause summary and mitigations

oncall-next: acknowledged, will own until 14:00 UTC tomorrow and start the postmortem doc.

alex: closing active paging channel. will attach logs + graphs to incident doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:
